bullets.title: NVDA: $500B AI infrastructure financing platform – Wells Fargo OW $315, MS riterates Top Pick $288
bullets.body: NVDA confirmed a partnership with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize $500B+ in third-party AI infrastructure financing. Wells Fargo reiterates Overweight with $315 PT; Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore sees 10%+ FY29 EPS upside from a revenue-share annuity at ~100% gross margin and reiterates Top Pick at $288, noting the structure shifts capital risk to third parties while preserving 25% NVDA co-investment upside. NVDA also maintains one of the lowest forward P/E multiples in semis heading into a strong product cycle.

bullets.title: NVDA: Rubin Ultra HBM tiering, $91B Q2 guide, and upcoming earnings setup
bullets.body: JPMorgan buyside survey ahead of NVDA's F2Q27 earnings (Aug 26, $91B revenue guide) focuses on hyperscale vs. ACIE segment breakdown, gross margin at 75%, and memory stock catalyst potential. MS notes Rubin Ultra likely features tiered HBM specs (HBM4e 8Hi high-end, HBM4 12Hi/8Hi lower-end) to manage HBM4 capacity shortages — reducing memory content per chip but boosting chip shipment volumes.

bullets.title: Memory: JPM raises TAM 4-8%, sees DRAM/NAND shortage through 2028; HBM pricing +42% y/y
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Jay Kwon lifts FY26-28E memory TAM forecasts by 4-8% and sees supply/demand shortage worsening through 2028, especially DRAM. HBM pricing revised up to +42% y/y supported by longer 8Hi cycle and slower 12Hi ramp. Valuations seen as attractive with upside to shareholder returns; SNDK analyst day upcoming as a near-term catalyst.

bullets.title: INTC: Upsized $20B secondary priced at $95, 6.5% discount
bullets.body: Intel raised $20B in an upsized secondary offering (vs. $15B target) priced at $95/share, a 6.5% discount to the prior close. Wolfe Research flagged the INTC secondary as a discussion topic for its Aug 14 semiconductor webcast. The deal represents a significant equity issuance event to watch for post-offering price pressure.

bullets.title: TSM/TSEM: Sony-TSMC $4.7B JV for image sensors; CoWoS capacity doubling annually
bullets.body: TSMC and Sony officially announced a $4.7B joint venture ('Advanced Vision') in Kumamoto, Japan for next-gen smartphone image sensors, with Sony contributing $2.92B (controlling stake) and TSMC $1.77B; volume production targets 2029. Separately, TSMC VP Jun He reports CoWoS capacity has doubled each of the last 3 years, now operating 10 advanced packaging plants, with 5.5x reticle CoWoS in mass production at 98%+ yields — 'very close' to meeting demand but not yet satisfied.

bullets.title: NXP Semiconductors (NXPI): KeyBanc forum takeaways – book-to-bill >1, Kinara pipeline $1.5B record
bullets.body: At the KeyBanc Technology Leadership Forum, NXPI cited improved business environment vs. 90 days ago, book-to-bill solidly above 1 across all end markets, and distribution inventory normalizing to 11-week target. Kinara opportunity pipeline grew to $1.5B (fastest in company history); accelerated auto growth drivers now ~50% of auto revenue. Next-gen auto products (S32N, K5) to drive revenue from late 2027. Targeted price increases due to input cost inflation expected to be more material in H2 2026.

bullets.title: AAPL: Glass-centric 2027 iPhone on track, countering Jefferies downgrade; Hedgeye flips short
bullets.body: A source report confirms Apple's glass-centric 20th-anniversary iPhone (2027) remains on track, cited as a direct refutation of the Jefferies downgrade thesis — a positive read for Corning (GLW) as glass supplier. Separately, Hedgeye is flipping AAPL from long to short, citing China reports of iPhone 18 price hikes of 10-23% and a foldable Ultra priced $400 above prior models ($2,223-$2,667), arguing the margin-protection strategy could backfire materially with 23% downside flagged.

bullets.title: GLW: Morgan Stanley flags capacity tightness as bullish; buy-the-dip recommended
bullets.body: MS notes GLW's hyperscaler LTAs are absorbing all available fiber capacity, limiting near-term pricing upside vs. peers like Fujikura (which achieved ~25% like-for-like price increases). GLW capex rising to 12.6% of sales in 2H FY26. The NVDA-backed long-haul fiber build (16 routes, 1,728 fibers/route) extends AI fiber demand beyond data centers. MS recommends buying the dip.

bullets.title: AVGO/MRVL: JPM survey ahead of Aug-Sept earnings; AI silicon wins in focus
bullets.body: JPMorgan's buyside survey ahead of AVGO's F3Q26 earnings (Sept 2) asks whether AVGO raises its F27 AI guide above $100B and announces new AI project wins. For MRVL (F2Q27 due Aug 27), focus is on data center revenue, gross margins, and potential new AI silicon wins. Both names flagged as best-positioned for AI-driven spending alongside NVDA and MU.

bullets.title: PI (Everpure): Second top-5 hyperscaler design win; stock hits $108
bullets.body: Everpure announced a second major hyperscaler Master Supply Agreement (likely Oracle) within one day of MS's upgrade to Overweight. DirectFlash technology validated for large-scale AI/cloud applications; hyperscale gross margins guided at 75-85% vs. 90%+ for Meta. JPM notes management's conservative outlook appears overly cautious per channel checks.

bullets.title: HIMS: Branded GLP-1 drives reacceleration but EBITDA guidance cut to fund growth; -6.9% pre-mkt
bullets.body: Truist post-call Q&A: branded GLP-1 was the primary 2Q26 U.S. growth driver with similar dollar EBITDA contribution per subscriber vs. compounded GLP-1. HIMS lowered 2026 EBITDA guidance ceiling to fund affordability initiatives, AI, and international expansion. Eucalyptus contributed ~$40M in one month; international expected near EBITDA break-even. Gross margin headwinds expected in 2H26 as weight loss/international mix grows.

bullets.title: PLTR: DA Davidson bull thesis – 93% growth, 50x forward CF, durable moat vs. OpenAI/Anthropic
bullets.body: DA Davidson argues Palantir deserves premium valuation at ~50x forward cash flow, citing 93% revenue growth, ~150% commercial and ~90% government growth, and a competitive moat from forward-deployed engineers, proprietary ontology, and outcome-based pricing. 50-70% compound growth seen as underwritable for 3-5 years; Snowflake, Datadog, and CrowdStrike cited as closest comparables but Palantir argued to deserve a premium.

bullets.title: CVLT: KeyBanc forum – 19% subscription ARR growth, 10-yr high margins, H2 SaaS acceleration
bullets.body: CommVault guided 19% y/y subscription ARR growth for FY26 with SaaS at 38% y/y growth in Q1 and 70% gross margins. EBIT margin hit a 10-year high of ~23% in Q1. Significant H2 ARR acceleration expected from SaaS cross-sell; share buybacks to accelerate in Q2, targeting at least 60% of FCF returned.

bullets.title: NOK: Jefferies top pick into year-end; 30%+ 2027 earnings growth, stock at 1-year lows
bullets.body: Jefferies names Nokia a top EU semis pick for the next 6 months alongside IFX, citing 25-28% NI growth running well ahead of management's 6-8% CAGR guidance. Consensus-beating upgrades expected at Q3 and Q4; orders/backlog rising rapidly in optical and data center switching. Stock at €8, down on momentum unwind and index fund selling, trading at April lows despite an upgraded IP+Optical guide and record order intake. ECOC conference Sept 20-24 seen as sector catalyst.

bullets.title: FSLR: Baird upgrades to outperform, raises PT to $318 from $205
bullets.body: Baird upgraded First Solar to outperform from neutral and raised its price target to $318 from $205 (vs. FactSet average ~$277). Stock was +3.5% pre-market on the upgrade.

bullets.title: CEG/VST/TLN/GEV/VRT: Political risk to data-center approvals from rising electricity bills
bullets.body: Roth is surveying to assess whether rising electricity costs are generating political resistance to data-center buildout approvals in PJM and ERCOT regions — a potential headwind for power-sector names. The survey will measure consumer blame attribution to AI data centers and identify concessions needed to convert opposition to support.

bullets.title: AFRM: Reports Aug 27; JPM expects 28%+ GMV growth, trading at historical average valuation
bullets.body: JPMorgan previews AFRM's F4Q26 (Aug 27): base case is 28%+ GMV growth, 4.0% RLTC margins, ~30% adjusted operating margins. AFRM has beaten Street GMV estimates by 4.5% over last 8 quarters; Intuit partnership adds ~2ppts to GMV growth. Stock trading at 10x NTM gross profit, in line with historical averages.

bullets.title: MELI: JPM credit review – Brazil +75% y/y, Mexico +85% y/y, but Brazil complaints index worsens
bullets.body: JPMorgan's monthly MELI credit review shows Argentina gross loans $1.4B (+9% m/m, +27% y/y) with improving NPLs; Brazil book R$48.3B (+75% y/y); Mexico loan book +85% y/y and +12% q/q in 1Q26, accelerating from 73% in 4Q25. Negative: MELI's Brazil complaints ranking worsened to 5th highest per 1M users in 2Q26 vs. 9th previously.

bullets.title: APP (AppLovin): BofA downgrade, stock -5.3% at 52-week lows; -2.3% pre-market
bullets.body: AppLovin was downgraded by BofA, contributing to a -2.3% pre-market decline. The stock hit a 52-week low with a -29.6% trailing drawdown, per StreetAccount's 52-week highs/lows screen.

bullets.title: NET: $2.175B convertible offering priced; FWONK $600M convertible also priced
bullets.body: Cloudflare (NET) priced a $2.175B convertible note offering on August 11. Liberty Media Formula One (FWONK) priced a $600M convertible. Both are notable capital markets events for the portfolio.
